summary: Baileys fork stamps charcode-obfuscated author URL into outbound WhatsApp message previews
details: alipclutch-baileys is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp library. In lib/Socket/messages-send.js (around line 425 and line 436), the image/reel/video preview builders set the outgoing message's `sourceUrl` field to a hardcoded literal constructed via String.fromCharCode(...) that decodes to https://fiora.nixel.my.id/. The destination is hidden from plain-text review by charcode encoding rather than appearing as a normal URL string, and it is stamped into every message the consumer's bot sends through these builders. The behavior uses the installer's WhatsApp session to brand outbound content with an author-controlled URL, but it does not read installer credentials, filesystem contents, or environment variables, does not exfiltrate caller data to the author, and does not fetch or execute remote code.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
